package audio

// ddsonic's contract with go-librespot's audio key provider and chunked
// reader, at the pinned version. See
// docs/ddsonic/design/spotify-token-coordinator.md, 4.3 and 14.5.

import (
	"context"
	"errors"
	"io"
	"net"
	"net/http"
	"sync"
	"testing"
	"time"

	librespot "github.com/devgianlu/go-librespot"
	"github.com/devgianlu/go-librespot/ap"
)

// stalledConn accepts nothing: its first Write blocks until it is closed.
type stalledConn struct {
	entered, closed chan struct{}
	enter, shut     sync.Once
}

func newStalledConn() *stalledConn {
	return &stalledConn{entered: make(chan struct{}), closed: make(chan struct{})}
}
func (c *stalledConn) Read([]byte) (int, error) { return 0, io.EOF }
func (c *stalledConn) Write([]byte) (int, error) {
	c.enter.Do(func() { close(c.entered) })
	<-c.closed
	return 0, io.ErrClosedPipe
}
func (c *stalledConn) Close() error                     { c.shut.Do(func() { close(c.closed) }); return nil }
func (c *stalledConn) LocalAddr() net.Addr              { return nil }
func (c *stalledConn) RemoteAddr() net.Addr             { return nil }
func (c *stalledConn) SetDeadline(time.Time) error      { return nil }
func (c *stalledConn) SetReadDeadline(time.Time) error  { return nil }
func (c *stalledConn) SetWriteDeadline(time.Time) error { return nil }

// stalledPump is a key provider whose writer is inside a Send that does not
// return, with one more Request queued behind it on ctx2. second receives
// that Request's result.
func stalledPump(t *testing.T, ctx2 context.Context) (a *ap.Accesspoint, second chan error) {
	t.Helper()
	conn := newStalledConn()
	a = ap.DDSonicContractAP(conn)
	p := NewAudioKeyProvider(&librespot.NullLogger{}, a)
	ctx1, cancel1 := context.WithCancel(context.Background())
	first := make(chan error, 1)
	go func() { _, err := p.Request(ctx1, make([]byte, 16), make([]byte, 20)); first <- err }()
	select {
	case <-conn.entered:
	case <-time.After(5 * time.Second):
		t.Fatal("the key pump did not reach its Send")
	}
	cancel1()
	<-first
	second = make(chan error, 1)
	go func() { _, err := p.Request(ctx2, make([]byte, 16), make([]byte, 20)); second <- err }()
	t.Cleanup(a.Close)
	return a, second
}

// STOP if this fails: with patch 0002, a Request queued behind a stalled
// write, and not yet committed, ends with its context (the pre-commit
// cancellation the owners accepted). v0.9.1 held it until the access point
// closed.
func TestDDSonicContractKeyRequestFollowsContextBeforeCommit(t *testing.T) {
	ctx2, cancel2 := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 20*time.Millisecond)
	t.Cleanup(cancel2)
	_, second := stalledPump(t, ctx2)
	select {
	case err := <-second:
		if !errors.Is(err, context.DeadlineExceeded) {
			t.Fatalf("the queued Request = %v, want its context's DeadlineExceeded", err)
		}
	case <-time.After(5 * time.Second):
		t.Fatal("the queued Request did not end with its context")
	}
}

// STOP if this fails: a Request stalled behind the writer, on a context that
// does not end, is released when a Close of the access point begins.
func TestDDSonicContractDoneReleasesKeyRequest(t *testing.T) {
	a, second := stalledPump(t, context.Background())
	go a.Close()
	select {
	case err := <-second:
		if !errors.Is(err, ap.ErrAccesspointClosed) {
			t.Fatalf("the released Request = %v, want ap.ErrAccesspointClosed", err)
		}
	case <-time.After(5 * time.Second):
		t.Fatal("the access point's Close did not release the stalled Request")
	}
}

// STOP if this fails: a setup that starts on a retired bundle must fail at
// once.
func TestDDSonicContractRequestAfterCloseFails(t *testing.T) {
	a := ap.DDSonicContractAP(newStalledConn())
	p := NewAudioKeyProvider(&librespot.NullLogger{}, a)
	a.Close()
	done := make(chan error, 1)
	go func() { _, err := p.Request(context.Background(), make([]byte, 16), make([]byte, 20)); done <- err }()
	select {
	case err := <-done:
		if !errors.Is(err, ap.ErrAccesspointClosed) {
			t.Fatalf("a Request after Close = %v, want ap.ErrAccesspointClosed", err)
		}
	case <-time.After(5 * time.Second):
		t.Fatal("a Request made after Close did not fail at once")
	}
}

// lifetimeTransport is ddsonic's stream transport in miniature: every
// request is put on the stream's own context.
type lifetimeTransport struct {
	life    context.Context
	entered chan struct{}
	once    *sync.Once
}

func (t lifetimeTransport) RoundTrip(r *http.Request) (*http.Response, error) {
	r = r.Clone(t.life)
	t.once.Do(func() { close(t.entered) })
	<-r.Context().Done()
	return nil, r.Context().Err()
}

func firstChunk(t *testing.T) (cancelLife context.CancelFunc, finished chan error) {
	t.Helper()
	life, cancel := context.WithCancel(context.Background())
	t.Cleanup(cancel)
	entered := make(chan struct{})
	finished = make(chan error, 1)
	client := &http.Client{Transport: lifetimeTransport{life, entered, new(sync.Once)}}
	go func() {
		_, err := NewHttpChunkedReader(&librespot.NullLogger{}, client, "https://synthetic.invalid/audio")
		finished <- err
	}()
	select {
	case <-entered:
	case <-time.After(5 * time.Second):
		t.Fatal("the chunked reader did not ask for its first chunk")
	}
	return cancel, finished
}

// A reviewed expectation: the chunked reader's first request is made on a
// context of its own, so nothing a stream setup's context does ends it. It
// is why every unaccepted track open ends its HTTP lifetime itself.
func TestDDSonicContractFirstChunkIgnoresSetupContext(t *testing.T) {
	setup, cancelSetup := context.WithCancel(context.Background())
	_, finished := firstChunk(t)
	cancelSetup() // a setup context, as NewStream's caller would end it
	<-setup.Done()
	select {
	case err := <-finished:
		t.Fatalf("EXPECTATION CHANGED: the first chunk request ended without its client's context: %v", err)
	case <-time.After(50 * time.Millisecond):
	}
}

// STOP if this fails: the open handle would no longer release a stalled
// open. Ending the context the client puts on its requests ends the first
// chunk request, and the reader's constructor returns an error.
func TestDDSonicContractClientContextEndsFirstChunk(t *testing.T) {
	cancelLife, finished := firstChunk(t)
	cancelLife()
	select {
	case err := <-finished:
		if err == nil {
			t.Fatal("the chunked reader succeeded with its first request cancelled")
		}
	case <-time.After(5 * time.Second):
		t.Fatal("ending the client's context did not end the first chunk request")
	}
}
